rationale: Y covers more of the ground-truth threads with genuine depth: it independently verifies the version=1/2/default kernel-resolution behavior against the real kernels library (matching wtomin's question), extends RuixiangMa's SM90-gating concern with cross-capability simulation catching the Blackwell over-inclusion bug, and surfaces a real varlen-assumption gap closely related to the piecewise crash RuixiangMa found. X covers the two 'resolved' bugs (piecewise crash, SM90 gate) reasonably but pads its output with speculative claim-verified/refuted commentary on PR marketing language that adds little review value and isn't grounded in reviewer concerns. Both are highly actionable with concrete file/line references, X slightly more so via literal suggestion diffs, but Y's findings are more empirically grounded (actual timing, Hub API queries) giving it higher precision.
